evidence.note: Agent explicitly decides a real C frontend is 'not feasible' and builds a driver that forwards compilation to clang/gcc. No compiler-feature staging (return-int → expressions → variables → …) is ever conceived; the whole language is bypassed rather than decomposed.

After clang is absent, it pivots the wrapper to invoke the target-specific gcc binary directly. Work is organized around making the pass-through driver satisfy the harness check, not around language-feature milestones.

Iteration is driven purely by which individual test files fail (page-boundary sidecar asm, dg-options parsing) — debugging a gcc-forwarding wrapper, not certifying ordered compiler features against test subsets.
Final push chases a single remaining gcc dg-option guard and declares done at 780/780. No dependency-ordered milestone plan, no per-feature done-signals ever appear across the entire trajectory.

reasoning: The agent did not build a compiler and therefore produced no feature-staged progression at all — it substituted a gcc-forwarding driver and then debugged that wrapper test-by-test. This matches the level-0 anchor: no ordering tied to language-feature dependencies and no per-milestone completion criteria; the incremental work observed is wrapper-fixing, not milestone decomposition of compiler stages.
